messages:
alex: Heads up — scheduling a staged NIC firmware window in apac-west1 next Tue 00:30–03:30 UTC. Targeting 3 cohorts (rack groups) to avoid capacity cliff. Will drain, reboot, and validate NVMe + NIC firmware.

maria: Is this going to affect Dedicated pools or just hosted? Need to know for customer comms/SLA.

tariq: Hosted only. Dedicated pools are pinned to customer clusters and not in this cohort. I'll double-check mapping, but I flagged the cohort label `apac-west1-cohort-b` to avoid overlap.

josh: Thanks. Can we route queued/long-running jobs off these nodes before drain? Suggest set drain timeout to 10m and force after 20m. Also will warm prefix cache after bringup.

alex: Plan: run `kubectl cordon` + `kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=600` per node, then reboot, then smoke test w/ 2 small inference jobs. If smoke ok, uncordon. Will do canary of 2 nodes first.

maria: Any cost impact from burst capacity (if we backfill into eu pools)? Finance asked for estimated delta.

josh: Backfill into eu-west1 will add ~2.5% GPU hour usage for that 3h window; estimate ~$1.2k extra in gross runcost for the event (before discounts).

sre-lead: Also note networking egress will spike during KV cache warmups — watch egress QPS and set temporary egress throttle if we hit thresholds. I set alert `egress.apac-west1.spike` to p0.

ops-bot: schedule created: maintenance/apac-west1-nic-fw/2026-06-15T00:30Z -> created by alex. Notifying oncall rotation.

oncall-bot: @oncall rotation for 2026-06-15: tariq (primary), maria (secondary). Paging window enabled 00:30-04:00 UTC.

tariq: For routing: we'll add a short policy to route new requests to eu and fallback to apac on capacity ok. Patch to router config ready, will deploy canary with `route:prefer_region=eu` flag.

maria: Customer comms draft: "Planned maintenance in apac-west1; transient capacity shifts may increase latency for customers in APAC for ~3 hours. Dedicated customers unaffected." Will send after Alex + SRE confirm.

alex: Confirmed. Action items: (1) josh run canary drain tonight in staging, (2) tariq push router canary 30m before window, (3) maria send comms 2h before window, (4) oncall watch egress alerts.

josh: Canary drain in staging done — logs look clean, one pod needed `--force` due to stuck PV; noted in runbook. Command used:
```
kubectl drain node-az3-01 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=600
ssh node-az3-01 sudo reboot
```

sre-lead: I'll shadow the run. If we see >5% latency regression on the canary, abort and roll forward with smaller cohorts.

alex: Roger. Final note — prefer rolling window to start at 00:30 UTC to hit local night in APAC. Will post postmortem if anything leaks. :raised_hands:
